messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] hosted-runtime: kvcache memory usage spike -> OOMs observed (5 events) on pool-hosted-3 in 2m. severity: high. logs: https://logs.internal/r/xyz123 metric: kvcache_used_gb=93%, evictions=0. Alert: OOM kill on process redwood-runtime

morgan (oncall): seeing increased 5xx from hosted endpoints, any known deploys? :eyes:

lee (runtime): no deploys from runtime team in last hour. traffic looks normal but context length distribution has long tail spiking. Likely runaway prompt expansion + continuous batching prefetch filling KV maps.

devon (sre): pulling node logs now. early signs show rapid kvmap growth for a handful of sessions, windows not evicting.

morgan (oncall): customers reporting 502/524 on generation endpoints. @emily (cs) can you list impacted customers?

emily (cs): seeing support tickets from two customers (acme-ai, learninglabs). both high-volume chat apps. tickets reference intermittent 502s since ~10m ago. I put them on incident list.

lee (runtime): quick triage: continuous-batching prefetch enabled on model redwood-ggml-large in hosted pool. prefetch config recently widened batch_window_ms from 50 -> 150 in rollout earlier today. hypothesis: longer window + long prompts -> kv cache blowup and eviction starvation.

devon (sre): we should throttle prefetch and reduce batch window immediately. can we flip config on pool-hosted-3?

lee (runtime): yes. prepared a minimal hotfix patch, will deploy to pool-hosted-3 only:

```
# hotfix: reduce prefetch aggressiveness
prefetch.enabled: false
batching.batch_window_ms: 30
kvcache.max_entries_per_session: 20000
```

morgan (oncall): execute and watch metrics. if memory back to normal route traffic back.

opsbot: Running rollout job: rollout/patch-hotfix-456 -> targeted pools: pool-hosted-3. job id: roll-456.

opsbot: Rollout step 1 -> apply config to 10% of nodes in pool-hosted-3.

devon (sre): logs show OOMs continuing on nodes outside the 10% cut. need faster mitigation: consider immediate session-level eviction and fallback routing.

lee (runtime): enabling aggressive session eviction for pool-hosted-3 now: `kvcache.eviction_policy: aggressive` and apply traffic split to fallback model redwood-small-quant v1 (lower mem).

```
# traffic split
route.hosted/model: redwood-ggml-large@0.0. -> 0.6
route.hosted/model: redwood-small-quant@0.0 -> 0.4
```

morgan (oncall): @sanjay (eng-ml) any concerns about quality from fallback model?

sanjay (eng-ml): small quant will degrade quality for some prompts but avoids OOMs. prefer degrade over customer errors. can we target non-critical customers first?

emily (cs): acme-ai flagged as critical SLA. they need continuity. please prioritize them for fallback routing if necessary.

lee (runtime): applied aggressive eviction and traffic split to pool-hosted-3; also killed a couple of runaway sessions manually (session ids: s-1245, s-1299).

opsbot: Rollout progress: 10% -> 100% on pool-hosted-3. patch applied.

devon (sre): memory metrics trending down. kvcache_used_gb went from 93% -> 68% in 3m. OOMs stopped. eviction rate increased as expected.

morgan (oncall): monitoring latency/5xx. any residual customer impact?

emily (cs): acme-ai reports reduced errors after ~5m, one remaining degraded quality complaint from learninglabs (seeing lower token coherence). they accepted temporary fallback.

lee (runtime): next steps: revert prefetch widening rollout globally, add tighter guardrails on prefetch window and kvmap caps, and ship a targeted fix to make prefetch opt-in per-customer. need a patch PR and a canary.

sanjay (eng-ml): propose additional heuristics: abort prefetch when input token count > 4096 and cap kvcache entries per session at 50k. also add telemetry to track prefix amplification.

devon (sre): create incident runbook update: 1) hotpatch reduce prefetch/ batch_window 2) traffic split to low-mem model 3) enable aggressive eviction 4) manual kill for runaway sessions 5) notify CS + affected customers.

morgan (oncall): handing off to night oncall @lee. I'll stay for 15m for questions then sign off. please update incident channel when stabilized. :white_check_mark:

lee (runtime): taking handoff. created follow-up ticket INF-789 with root-cause hypothesis and action items. linking logs and charts: https://metrics.internal/d/abc-kvcache

emily (cs): I've sent proactive notifications to acme-ai and learninglabs outlining mitigation and expected timeline.

morgan (oncall): postmortem requested. assign to runtime+ml+sre. include timeline, config diffs, and recommended prefetch safe defaults.

opsbot: Incident status -> mitigated. impact: degraded quality for subset (fallback), 502 spikes mitigated, OOMs resolved. severity -> P1 -> downgraded to P2 pending postmortem.

lee (runtime): quick snippet of the config diff applied in hotfix (for postmortem):
```
- prefetch.enabled: true
- batching.batch_window_ms: 150
+ prefetch.enabled: false
+ batching.batch_window_ms: 30
+ kvcache.max_entries_per_session: 20000
```

morgan (oncall): thanks team. leave notes in INF-789 and tag me. I'll close after postmortem review. :bow:
